programs.title: X-Ray Earth
programs.desc: Scientists examine a large fault line off the coast of the Pacific Northwest and the possible devastation that could result from a megaquake and tsunami.

programs.title: Hostile Planet
programs.desc: Deserts are getting even hotter, drier and bigger, yet a host of remarkable animals still survive in the harshest of conditions, including cunning hyenas, pint-sized meerkats and sand-dwelling spiders.

programs.title: Hostile Planet
programs.desc: Jungles comprise the most diverse habitats on Earth in which only the resilient species can triumph; these jungle species include jaguars, caimans, gibbons, orangutans, spectral tarsiers, hummingbirds and parasites.

programs.title: Hostile Planet
programs.desc: In the grasslands, animals endure freezes, fires, floods and droughts; bull elephants clash in mating battles; cheetahs and gazelles engage in a predator-and-prey dance in the Kenyan savanna; bison battle a blizzard while being pursued by wolves.

programs.title: Hostile Planet
programs.desc: Delving beneath the surface of the Earth's oceans to uncover a world of extraordinary extremes, including crushing depths, stormy coasts, vast blue deserts, and crowded reefs; how seals fend off sharks; how orcas fight to survive.

programs.title: Hostile Planet
programs.desc: The highest mountains on Earth are home to snow leopards, golden eagles, mountain goats, barnacle goslings, and gelada monkeys; only the toughest of animals can endure the extreme weather, scarce food supplies and limited oxygen on these peaks.
